dedupe_keys.name: a dataset of 5 million city trees from 63 us cities dryad

description: This dataset standardises city and neighbourhood tree inventories from 63 of the largest US cities into 5,660,237 tree records with a common set of 28 columns. Dakota McCoy, Benjamin Goulet-Scott and co-authors from Stanford, Harvard, Cornell, Worcester Polytechnic Institute and the Biota of North America Program published it on Dryad in June 2022 (updated August 2022) with a primary article in eLife. Each datasheet gives tree location, species, nativity status (native or introduced), health, size, whether the tree is in a park or urban area and more. Coverage is 63 US cities. Format and access: one standardised table per city downloaded from Dryad. Licence: CC0-1.0; free. Caveats: the source inventories differ in date, completeness and whether they include park trees, so cross-city comparisons need care. It supports urban heat, carbon and storm-damage exposure studies and planning of green infrastructure across cities. Related catalogue records are the North American urban tree dataset, a similar 30-city compilation, and the NYC 2015 Street Tree Census, one of the inventories such sets draw on.
